method: A person-equivalent review: the screenshot images were opened and read. Only the entries below count as visually verified, and only for the tab named.

inspected.observed: three hosts with their sourcetypes; phase table BASELINE 12, ONSET 9, SPREAD 16, CONTAINMENT 8, RECOVERY 12; Status by phase shows normal, then blocked and degraded, then blocked with restored, then normal and restored; phase report table populated

Status by phase normal, degraded, restored; mstats panels render real metric data (in_octets, out_octets, avgLatencyMs, packetLossPct and others) from the metric index. Limits: byte counters dominate the scale so small gauges look flat; event panels show only zscaler:zia because the other sourcetypes are metrics in the metric index; the time-trend chart is a single point on a fast bounded run

after the fix: Events by source (steady-state scenario: no incident); Events by phase and source shows load rising in PEAK across five sources and falling in COOLDOWN. Before the fix the generic chart labelled every source During incident (defect, fixed). Leftover: the table title Impact events (everything after the baseline) reads oddly for a no-incident scenario
cisco:ise:syslog and netspout:scenario:state both present; Status by phase healthy and normal, then a large degraded and impaired block (the ISE failure spike), then restored; phase report populated

ThousandEyes metrics from the metric index: avgLatencyMs rises in the incident phase, httpCode average rises with 504, packetLossPct and tcpConnectTime present; Status by phase healthy, impaired, healthy
inspected.verdict: meaningful; confirms the ThousandEyes metric extraction fix

inspected.observed: after the fix: Measured indicator by phase charts temperature_c rising from about 4 to about 11 and back to about 4; Status by phase runs normal, excursion and alert_firing, mitigating and alert_acknowledged, recovered and alert_cleared

caveat: UCR-22.1.5 and UCR-8.1.1 were rendered before the measured-indicator panel was added, so their current views were not rendered; arch_nas_storage_cluster was re-rendered after the change but its screenshot was not inspected.
